subject: Console: scope for cost-slice drilldown + exception handling playbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Devon Raymond <devon@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Console: scope for cost-slice drilldown + exception handling playbook

Folks — looping you in. Acme (Devon) flagged a need for two things we currently don't expose cleanly in the Console:

1) Per-route "slice" drilldowns for cost and tail latency (they want to see cost by prompt template / model variant / tenant slice).
2) A standardized playbook for SLA exceptions: when a route exceeds tail latency or token-cost thresholds, what automations / fallbacks and customer-facing messages do we run?

Devon shared a short sample log and a rough mockup request (attached). They asked for an outline of what we can deliver in an early release (MVP) vs. what will be a roadmap item.

Constraints I want us to think about up front:
- Data cardinality: customers will want arbitrary slices (route + prompt-template + model variant). We can't precompute everything.
- Latency: any added telemetry shouldn't add request-side latency.
- Ownership: who owns the UX + runbook for exception notifications vs. infra-level mitigations?

Proposed initial deliverables (MVP suggestion):
- Per-route breakdown in Console UI for last 24h/7d with token-cost and p90/p99 latency. Sampling-based drilldown to a configurable per-route sample rate.
- Exception playbook doc (internal + customer-facing summary) that maps an exception to steps: auto-fallback to cheaper model variant, temporary rate-limits, and a CS notification template.

Questions for Product/Eng: what's technically realistic in a 6-8 week sprint vs. longer-term? Laura, any red flags on telemetry or query cost? Stephanie, what should the customer-facing summary look like?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Devon Raymond <devon@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console: scope for cost-slice drilldown + exception handling playbook

Thanks Marcus — good summary and useful prompt from Acme. A few quick thoughts from Product: 

- MVP definition: I agree with your two buckets (UI + playbook). For the first pass I think we should scope to:
  * Per-route panel showing aggregated token cost, requests, p50/p90/p99 latency for the last 24h and last 7d.
  * A sampling option that lets users capture detailed traces for a percentage of calls (1%/5%/10%), which powers the drilldown.
  * Simple filters for model variant and tenant tag.

- Playbook: I propose a one-page "Customer Incident Summary" + internal "Operator Runbook". The customer page is non-technical (what happened, expected impact, immediate mitigation), while the operator runbook contains the exact fallback flows, log locations, and rollback steps.

Open questions:
- Should the MVP include automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant, or just surface a one-click toggle? Auto-fallback reduces manual ops but increases risk if quality degrades.
- How do we surface cost attribution for multi-tenant requests? We need to decide whether per-tenant token attribution is 100% accurate or approximate (and call that out).

Linking a draft mockup and a Drive folder with Acme's sample logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-console-cost-playbook

Laura, can you comment on feasibility and an engineering estimate? Monica, can you confirm what Acme would consider an acceptable SLA notification cadence (immediate, 15m, 1h)?

— Stephanie
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console: scope for cost-slice drilldown + exception handling playbook

Thanks — this is a good framing. A couple of engineering notes / constraints: 

1) Telemetry and sampling: we can surface per-route aggregates cheaply if we emit summarized metrics (counts, token totals, latency histograms) to our metrics pipeline. For ad-hoc drilldowns, sampling is the right play — full per-request indexing will balloon storage and query cost. A 1-5% sampling rate should be sufficient to reconstruct p99s for high-volume routes; for low-volume routes we'll need fallback heuristics.

2) Attribution: per-tenant token attribution is tricky for multi-tenant requests or shared prompts. We can provide "best-effort" attribution (split by token-origin heuristics) but must label it as estimated. For legal/finance use cases, we should call out that reserved capacity customers can enable deterministic attribution via a flag (adds overhead).

3) Exception mitigation: auto-fallback can be implemented in two ways: server-side routing policy (preferred) or client-facing toggle. Server-side auto-fallback requires: model-variant health scoring, per-route fallback policy, and an opt-in flag per customer. It also requires QA on quality regression detection (we should wire a lightweight eval on a small set of golden prompts before switching permanently). Estimated effort: 3-4 sprints across runtime + control plane + console. MVP alternative (1 sprint): surface recommendations and a one-click fallback action that triggers a manual switch by operations.

4) Instrumentation timeline: I can put a small team on the sampling + metrics export work in the next sprint (2 engineers, 3 weeks) and then follow with a console-side panel (2 engineers, 3 weeks). The playbook doc is product-led and should be ready in Parallel.

Attachments: I included a small sample of what the exported exception log looks like (acme-exception-log-sample.txt).

I'll open OBS-2147 and attach a minimal tech spec. If we want auto-fallback in the MVP the timeline slips significantly.

— Laura
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Devon Raymond <devon@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Console: scope for cost-slice drilldown + exception handling playbook

Appreciate the fast replies and the pragmatic splits. To summarize action items: 

- Laura: create OBS-2147 (tech spec + estimate). Implement sampling export pipeline (2 engs, 3 weeks) — mark auto-fallback as RISKY and roadmap-level. Attach acme-exception-log-sample to the ticket.
- Stephanie: draft the one-page Customer Incident Summary + internal Operator Runbook. Link the Drive folder and make a customer-friendly PDF for Acme.
- Monica: confirm Acme's desired notification cadence and whether they'd opt into an opt-in fallback pilot.
- Devon (Acme): please confirm the top 3 slices you care about (they suggested: prompt-template, model-variant, tenant-tag) and whether 1-5% sampling would be acceptable for drilldowns.

I'll create a weekly 30m sync invite for this thread and link OBS-2147 in the calendar. If we keep auto-fallback out of the MVP, we should be able to ship the sampling + per-route panel and the playbook in ~6–8 weeks.

Thanks all — Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
